catalog_quote: In Semelai the domain of word stress is the final syllable and there is no secondary stress. Only phonological words bear stress. In the case of words bearing suffixes

audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-strict' final stress (final stress) with no secondary stress rests on the modern standard reference grammar (Kruspe 2004, CUP, 493 pp.), §2.2.2, whose exact wording ('the domain of word stress is the final syllable and there is no secondary stress. Only phonological words bear stress. In the case of words bearing suffixes, stress shifts from the root to the suffix') is present verbatim in our held Open Library search-inside snippet files of the archive.org scan, and is independently quoted with the same page (2004:40) in the held Kaufman & Himmelmann handbook chapter; StressTyp2's banked Kruspe 1999:59 passage says the same. The loanword snippet (Malay penultimate stress replaced by Semelai final stress, ku.ˈciɲ) further supports strict final stress. No better or competing description of Semelai prosody exists in Glottolog, Crossref or Minerva; no instrumental study foun
